Q: My customer says HDFC has no room rent limit. Is that a big deal?
Yes, it is a significant advantage. With Star Comprehensive at Rs.3,000/day room rent limit, if the patient takes a private room at Rs.6,000/day, they pay the Rs.3,000 difference AND face proportionate deductions on other items like surgeon fees and nursing. With HDFC Optima Restore, no room rent cap means no proportionate deductions. This matters most for patients in metro cities where hospital room rents are high.
Q: My customer wants maternity coverage. Which plan is best?

Q: My customer wants maternity coverage. Which plan is best?
HDFC Optima Restore has the shortest waiting period at 24 months and covers Rs.50,000. Star Comprehensive also covers Rs.50,000 but requires 36 months. Bajaj Health Guard covers Rs.40,000 after 24 months. Recommend HDFC if customer is planning a family within 2-3 years.
Q: Customer already had a claim this year. Their sum insured is used up. What to tell them?
If on HDFC Optima Restore, their Sum Insured automatically restores once for a different illness — no extra premium needed. They still have full coverage. If on Star or Bajaj, sum insured does not restore and they are unprotected for the rest of the year. This is the key selling point for Optima Restore with high-risk customers.

Step 1 — Internal Appeal: File a written appeal with the Claims Review Team within 15 days of rejection. Include the rejection letter reference number, a clear rebuttal with supporting medical documents, and a request for reconsideration. Expected response: 14 working days.

Step 2 — Grievance Officer: If the internal appeal is denied, write to the Grievance Officer. By IRDAI mandate, the insurer must respond within 14 days and resolve within 30 days.
Step 3 — IRDAI IGMS: Register the complaint on igms.irda.gov.in with your policy number, claim reference, and correspondence history. IRDAI monitors all unresolved complaints.
Step 4 — Insurance Ombudsman: Approach your regional Ombudsman if the complaint remains unresolved. The service is free. The Ombudsman can compel the insurer to pay valid claims. Apply within 1 year of the final rejection.

SECTION 2 — DEFINITIONS
2.1 Hospitalisation
Hospitalisation means admission to a Hospital for a minimum period of 24 consecutive hours for the purpose of receiving Inpatient Care. Day Care Procedures listed in Annexure III are exempt from the 24-hour requirement.
2.2 Pre-Existing Disease (PED)
Any condition, ailment, injury, or disease that the Insured Person was diagnosed with or received medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment for within 48 months prior to the first policy commencement date. This includes conditions for which symptoms were present even if not formally diagnosed.
2.3 Day Care Procedure

2.3 Day Care Procedure
A medical treatment or surgical procedure that requires less than 24 hours of hospitalisation due to advancement in medical technology. Only procedures listed in Annexure III qualify. Treatment must be performed in a Hospital or Day Care Centre with specialized infrastructure.
2.4 Cashless Facility
A facility where the Insured Person can receive treatment at a Network Hospital without paying the hospitalisation charges upfront. The Insurer directly settles the bill with the hospital, subject to policy terms and conditions and the pre-authorisation approval.
2.5 Co-Payment

2.5 Co-Payment
The fixed percentage of the admissible claim amount that the Insured Person is required to bear before the Insurer pays the remaining amount. Co-payment applies to all claims made by Insured Persons above 60 years of age.
SECTION 3 — COVERAGE / WHAT IS COVERED
3.1 Inpatient Hospitalisation
Medical expenses incurred for Hospitalisation for illness or injury are covered up to the Sum Insured. Coverage includes:
Room, boarding, and nursing expenses as per sub-limits in Section 3.4
Fees of surgeon, anaesthetist, medical practitioner, consultants, and specialists
Anaesthesia, blood, oxygen, operation theatre charges
Surgical appliances and medicines consumed during hospitalisation
Diagnostic tests, X-rays, dialysis, chemotherapy, and radiotherapy
3.2 Pre and Post Hospitalisation

Diagnostic tests, X-rays, dialysis, chemotherapy, and radiotherapy
3.2 Pre and Post Hospitalisation
Medical expenses incurred 30 days before hospitalisation and 60 days after discharge are covered, provided the expenses are directly related to the illness/injury for which hospitalisation occurred.
3.3 Day Care Procedures
All procedures listed in Annexure III are covered regardless of duration of hospitalisation, provided they are performed at a Network Hospital or Day Care Centre. Key procedures include: Cataract surgery, Chemotherapy, Dialysis, Lithotripsy, Tonsillectomy, and 400+ others.
3.4 Sub-Limits Table — Room Rent and Other Charges
3.5 AYUSH Treatment

3.4 Sub-Limits Table — Room Rent and Other Charges
3.5 AYUSH Treatment
Treatment under Ayurveda, Yoga, Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha, and Homeopathy (AYUSH) is covered when taken at a Government or NABH-accredited AYUSH Hospital for a minimum 24-hour admission. Coverage is within the overall Sum Insured.
3.6 Mental Health Coverage
In compliance with IRDAI Circular IRDAI/HLT/REG/CIR/166/09/2022, mental health conditions are covered on par with physical health conditions. Psychiatric hospitalisation, outpatient psychiatric consultations (within OPD limit), and prescribed mental health medications are covered. Sub-limits specific to mental health treatment are not applicable.
3.7 No Claim Bonus (NCB)

3.7 No Claim Bonus (NCB)
For every claim-free policy year, the Sum Insured increases by 10% at renewal at no additional premium. Maximum accumulated NCB is 50% of the original Sum Insured. If a claim is made in any year, the NCB reverts to 0%.
SECTION 4 — WAITING PERIODS
Specific Diseases with 24-Month Waiting Period include: Hernia, Hydrocele, Fistula, Piles, Sinusitis, Varicose veins, Tonsilitis, Hypertension, Diabetes Mellitus, Tumours (benign), Osteoporosis, and Gall bladder stones.
SECTION 5 — EXCLUSIONS / WHAT IS NOT COVERED
5.1 Permanent Exclusions
Cosmetic or aesthetic surgery including rhinoplasty, breast augmentation, liposuction, and hair transplant, unless necessitated by a covered accident
Self-inflicted injuries, attempted suicide, or substance abuse

Self-inflicted injuries, attempted suicide, or substance abuse
War, invasion, hostilities, or nuclear contamination
Experimental treatments not approved by the Indian Medical Council
Dental treatment and surgery unless required due to accidental injury
Spectacles, contact lenses, hearing aids, and external prosthetics (unless post-surgery)
Treatment for obesity or weight reduction
Treatment outside India
Non-allopathic treatments (except covered AYUSH as per Section 3.5)

Step 1: Inform the TPA / Insurance company at least 48 hours before planned hospitalisation, or within 24 hours of emergency admission.
Step 2: Show your Star Health e-card or policy card at the hospital insurance desk.

SECTION 8 — GRIEVANCE REDRESSAL
In the event of any grievance regarding claim settlement or policy terms, the following escalation matrix applies:
Level 1: Contact customer care at 1800-425-2255 (toll-free) or email customercare@starhealth.in. Response within 7 working days.
Level 2: Write to the Grievance Officer at grievance@starhealth.in. Resolution within 14 days as per IRDAI mandate.
